named_confounds: genre composition shift (juvenile/adventure overrepresented late, domestic_realist early)
date_confidence heterogeneity (low-confidence dates show negative contrast)
small early-period cells per genre (47-280 works)
author productivity higher among late works
rationale: 6766 works, each with exactly one passage, so the work rate is 0/1. Cutoff is 1876. Early works: 752; late works: 6014. I took the mean rate per genre and period, computed late minus early within each of the 8 genres, and averaged the 8 differences with equal weight. The estimate is +0.018, with a 95% bootstrap CI (2000 resamples within genre-period cells) of [-0.006, 0.041]. The CI includes zero. Genre results disagree: juvenile +0.05, other +0.07, sensation +0.04, but adventure, collection and domestic_realist slightly negative. Genre mix differs sharply by period: juvenile works make up 2128 of 6014 late works but only 84 of 752 early works, so the crude decade trend partly reflects composition. A WLS regression adjusting for genre, origin, date_confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with author-clustered SEs, gives +0.012, CI [-0.011, 0.034]. Split by date confidence: high +0.031, medium +0.026, low -0.013. n_editions is balanced across periods. Author productivity is somewhat higher among late works. The well-dated subsets lean positive but were not shown to be significant, and the early cells are small. Alternative explanations for the raw increase: the later corpus is weighted toward juvenile and adventure fiction, and errors in assigned dates. Cited passages are examples coded as distance/travel; they do not show a trend. Evidence for a robust shift is not sufficient, so I abstain.
